name: AP Italian Language and Culture
overview: AP Italian Language and Culture develops interpretive, interpersonal, and presentational communication in Italian at roughly an intermediate-to-advanced level, organized around six themes and the cultures of Italy and Italian-speaking communities, including Switzerland and the Italian diaspora. The course and exam were revised for 2026-27: students complete a research project during the year that feeds into the spoken part of the exam.
examMode: Fully digital in Bluebook from May 2027 (spoken responses recorded in the app)

sections.name: Section I, Question 1
sections.notes: 3 minutes to prepare and 3 minutes to present findings from the research project completed during the course.

sections.name: Section I, Question 2
sections.notes: Four pre-recorded questions about your project; 40 seconds to answer each.

sections.name: Section I, Question 3
sections.notes: Written argument using sources that present multiple viewpoints, including an audio source played twice.

sections.name: Section II, Part A
sections.notes: Questions on audio sources such as conversations, interviews, podcasts, and reports.

sections.name: Section II, Part B
sections.notes: Questions on print texts such as articles, letters, ads, literary excerpts, and charts.

skills.name: Interpretive communication
skills.description: Understand main ideas, details, purpose, and audience in written and audio texts.

skills.name: Interpersonal communication
skills.description: Respond spontaneously and appropriately to questions.

skills.name: Presentational communication
skills.description: Present information and arguments in organized speech and writing.

skills.name: Cultural comparison
skills.description: Connect products, practices, and perspectives of Italian-speaking communities to your own.

scoring.summary: Multiple choice (listening 25%, reading 25%) is half the score; the project presentation (20%), project Q&A (15%), and argumentative essay (15%) make up the other half. Free responses are scored holistically on task completion, development, organization, language control, and vocabulary. Klutch's practice tasks use a 5-point holistic scale modeled on that approach.

frqTypes.name: Argumentative essay
frqTypes.howScored: Klutch practice scale (holistic, 0–5): a clear thesis answering the question, effective use and citation of all sources, organized paragraphs with transitions, and accurate, varied grammar and vocabulary.

frqTypes.name: Project presentation
frqTypes.howScored: Klutch practice scale (holistic, 0–5): a clear organized presentation of research findings with cultural content and comparison, fluent delivery, and accurate language.

frqTypes.name: Project Q&A
frqTypes.howScored: Klutch practice scale (1 point per answer): each answer responds directly to the question, elaborates with detail, and uses appropriate register and accurate language.

strategy: Read the questions before each passage or audio so you know what to listen and look for.
Questions usually follow the order of the text; the last question often asks about purpose or audience.
In the essay, cite each source ('Secondo la fonte 1...') and state a clear position in the introduction.
Use connectors (tuttavia, inoltre, quindi, invece, benché + congiuntivo) and a range of tenses.
For the Q&A, answer the question in the first sentence, then add a reason and an example; fill the 40 seconds.
Rehearse your project presentation so you can deliver it from your outline without reading.
pitfalls: Choosing an answer because it repeats words from the text; the correct answer usually paraphrases.
Mixing up passato prossimo and imperfetto, or essere/avere as auxiliaries.
Using tu instead of Lei in formal situations.
Summarizing sources without taking a position in the essay.
